text:
maya: Quick heads-up — seeing intermittent partial-JSON errors in the Python SSE client when token refresh returns 401 mid-stream. Happens under load when the client is backpressured and read window is small.
kevin: ugh, seen that pattern before. do you have a minimal repro or logs?
maya: pasted a sanitized excerpt below. note chunk boundary cuts inside an object and then a reconnect/401 closes the socket. client raises JSONDecodeError.
maya: ```
...
{"id":"msg-42","text":"start...

kevin: (reaction: :eyes:) can you also share client buffer size and queue maxsize? and which lib — aiohttp or httpx?
maya: httpx + asyncio. queue maxsize=64, chunk read size = 4096. under CPU pressure we end up with ~30ms pauses, and the server sends a 401 during refresh which leads to abrupt socket close.
ryan: two problems here: 1) auth refresh closing stream mid-object, 2) client windowing + bounded queue drops progress (backpressure). solution idea: reassemble incremental JSON more robustly and avoid dropping partial frames — treat stream decoder as stateful and yield only full objects. also, when you get a non-2xx during streaming, attempt graceful resume using Last-Event-ID or a per-message ack id.
kevin: agreed. for Python we usually use an incremental JSON parser pattern: keep a buffer, append bytes, try to find top-level object boundaries (e.g., count braces) and only parse complete objects. here's a tiny sketch:```
async def sse_consume(stream):
    buf = b""
    async for chunk in stream.aiter_bytes():
        buf += chunk
        while True:
            obj, used = try_extract_json(buf)  # returns (bytes, count) or (None,0)
            if not obj:
                break
            buf = buf[used:]
            await output_queue.put(obj)
```
kevin: also set output_queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=256) and on put do `await output_queue.put(obj)` which will apply backpressure to reader. if you don't want backpressure blocking the HTTP read coroutine (risking deadlock), use a small in-memory queue + a disk spillover or backpressure signal to the runtime that pauses consumption.
maya: hmm runtime-level pause isn't trivial with httpx. Could we add a short grace window on auth refresh so the server doesn't cut connection immediately? like complete current event then return 401?
ryan: server-side change would be ideal but not always possible for customers. Client should tolerate mid-stream failures: 1) preserve partial buffer, 2) on reconnect request resume with Last-Event-ID or `Range: bytes=` header when supported, 3) if resume not available, re-request missing messages via explicit cursor id in query (we include message ids in events).
kevin: small practical patch I pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/987 (WIP) — it switches to a stateful incremental parser and increases default queue maxsize to 256. also adds a hook `on_stream_error(partial_buffer)` so callers can inspect/ship partial payloads.
maya: nice. can you ping review? @kevin please add a unit test that simulates a mid-chunk 401 and asserts we don't raise JSONDecodeError and we surface a partial buffer to the hook.
kevin: will do. ETA EOD.
dev-bot: CI started for branch fix/sse-partial-json-401 (build #4223)
maya: thanks. one more question — is there a recommended retry/backoff pattern for streaming reconnects? exponential backoff + jitter? or immediate short retry for auth-only failures?
ryan: auth-only failures: short immediate retry after refresh (<=1s), then exponential backoff. but cap total retries to avoid infinite loops. also add circuit-breaker if stream error rate high.
kevin: I'll add config knobs: `stream_retry_initial=0.5`, `stream_retry_max=30`, `max_stream_retries=6`.
maya: perfect. tagging this thread as resolved for now — I'll test the PR on our repro harness and report back. :thumbsup:
